previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, chronic hepatitis C cirrhosis, and high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for her third cycle of doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy. She tolerated treatment well with minimal nausea, supported by scheduled antiemetics including dexamethasone, ondansetron, and lorazepam. Due to a prior leukemoid reaction from Neulasta, she was transitioned to Neupogen, to be started 48 hours after chemotherapy completion. Her hemoglobin dropped to 6.6 g/dL, prompting a transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with no signs of infection or sickle cell crisis. Liver enzymes improved during admission, and her pain was well controlled with hydromorphone. She was discharged home with clear instructions on medication management, infection precautions, and follow-up care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with sickle cell disease, Hep C, and high-grade osteosarcoma 
of the left tibia s/p resection and cisplatin/doxorubicin C3D1 = 
___ who presented with nausea and left knee pain.  

ACTIVE ISSUES
# Nausea / Vomiting: Likely related to cisplatin/doxorubicin 
regimen. Scheduled anti-emetics at recent discharge to prevent 
delayed nausea encountered with cycle #1. Patient was treated 
initially with standing then with PRN compazine, and IV 
lorazepam and ondansetron for breakthrough, with good effect. 
Received IVF given dehydration and contraction alkalosis. 
Tolerating PO intake well by day of discharge.  

# Bilateral knee pain: Patient associates pain with prior sickle 
cell crises. Exam was unremarkable, and pain is deep. No ROM 
comprimise. Did not appear like septic joint. Treated initially 
with IV hydromorphone but later switched to PO pain regimen in 
light of possible oversedation with IV medications.

# Leukocytosis: Likely due to overresponse to neupogen (patient 
has history of this in past). No evidence of infection. UA 
negative. CXR without obvious consolidation or infiltrates. 
Blood culture negative. Patient's counts downtrending rapidly 
off neupogen towards expected nadir, so patient was given 
additional dose of filgrastim prior to discharge and was to be 
called by Heme/Onc for followup appointment on ___ for labs 
and additional filgrastim injection.

# Acute on chronic Anemia: Believed to be ___ chemo and sickle 
cell disease. Hgb fell to 6.9 so patient was transfused 1 unit 
antigen matched pRBC prior to discharge.

CHRONIC ISSUES  
# Sickle cell disease: With chronic hemolysis, functionally 
asplenic. Received hydroxyurea x 2d for leukocytosis 
post-neulasta after cycle #1. Continue folic acid per home 
regimen
  
# Left tibia osteosarcoma: Completed cycle #3 of 6 of 
chemotherapy No hydroxyurea  
(on hold through cycle #6).

# GERD: Continued ranitidine, and calcium Carbonate

# Chronic hepatitis C: RUQ U/S recently negative. Hep C viral 
load 170,262 IU/mL in ___.  

# Proteinuria: Continued lisinopril 2.5 mg daily
